changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 32435687 (the crown with one cell removed) has an AND/OR circuit of fan-in two with at most 14 gates on the promise
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 5) (v : Fin 5) => (32435687 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 14
changed.unlocks: whether one named graph sits on or under the open pair's line on the AND/OR side
changed.context: A search. We hold an AND/OR circuit of 15 gates (the crown less a cell in at most 4n - 5, at n = 5; computed). The crown itself costs exactly 15 (a checked row), and the removed cell drops one AND term that the crown's chain shares, so its prefix ORs may serve the cut row with one gate fewer; at side 4 the least value was one below the hand move. What a circuit of 14 decides: by checked rows alone, nothing (a saving of at most 14 - 8 = 6); with the n + m - 2 transfer, a conjecture, it puts the graph on or under the line. We hold no circuit of 14 gates; this is a search.

changed.title: Every circuit selecting a satisfying cyclic word needs NOT gates to distinguish incomparable block words
changed.statement:
∀ (n w k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 0 < k → k ≤ n → k ≤ w + 1 →
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∀ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (outBit : Fin n → Fin (I + C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C →
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C →
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let inputs := List.ofFn (fun addr : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(addr.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun b => addr.val.testBit b.val))
      let valid := fun (word : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun j => word ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
      (∃ word, valid word) →
        valid (fun pos => (C.wires inputs).getD (outBit pos).val false)) →
    1 + (n / k) * (Nat.choose k (k / 2) - 1) ≤ 2 ^ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C
changed.unlocks: prices negations needed by any circuit returning a valid solution on satisfiable tables
changed.context: Use floor(n/k) disjoint blocks. A table at each block start admits a subset of the middle-weight k-bit words, ignoring extra bits. Other rows accept all. Shrink one subset by deleting the current witness block until one word remains, then move on. All tables stay satisfiable. Each change exchanges incomparable block words, so reversing the chain gives an output drop at every step. If previous wires have D dropping steps, AND/OR add none. A NOT adds at most one per increasing interval, giving at most 2D+1. Start at zero drops.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 12059857 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 9 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (12059857 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: A saving of at least two gates under this side-5 graph's checked AND/OR floor of 11, one below a checked circuit with NOT gates of 10.
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 9 gates; this is a search. A circuit of at most 10 gates with NOT gates for this graph is a checked row. We see no class of equal rows or columns here and no single line whose negation would pay; a yes would be a kind of saving we have not seen. Give a gate list of AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two, at most 9 gates, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. An exhausted search is a report, not a proof.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 841213 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 12 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (841213 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 12
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 13 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 12; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 4. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: No AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 53 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 24 vertices with 44 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. This side says the best circuit we know cannot be beaten by one gate: a finite search with a certificate the kernel replays, or an argument by restricting one vertex at a time down to smaller graphs whose sizes are checked. Size: unknown. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
